an1.1:2.1: Technically, it is not the sight that “occupies” the mind (literally “having invaded, remains”), but the unskillful qualities provoked by the sight ([an8.63:1.7]()). Hence this does not occur for one free of desire ([an6.55:17.1]()). As to what might have prompted such a strong statement, at [an5.55]() a similar passage is spoken in response to a mother and son, who, while ordained as monk and nun, had sex with each other. Elsewhere, it is said that possessions, honor, and popularity have an even more powerful effect on the mind ([sn17.21](), [sn17.22]()).
